title: Tuning and temperament, from the monochord and the pitch pipe to equal temperament
about: How the pitches of a scale were fixed, in Greece, China, India, the Arabic-speaking world and Europe, from about 500 BC to 1722: the problems that the methods met, what made each answer possible, and the philosophy of number that stood beside them. A seed drafted by a language model from memory: every statement is of grade C until a person confirms it against a source. Dates before 1582 are Julian; years BC are astronomical (239 BC is -0238). Periods' bounds are conventions.

name: Warring States period
summary: By one common convention, 475 to 221 BC; other conventions begin it in 453 or 403 BC.

name: Baroque era in music
summary: A convention of music history: about 1600 to about 1750.

name: The Pythagoreans
summary: The community founded by Pythagoras at Croton and those who followed its teaching.

name: The monochord
summary: One string over a ruled board with a movable bridge: a ratio of lengths is heard as an interval.

name: Pitch pipes
summary: Tubes of set lengths that give the standard pitches, the lü.

name: Chime bells
summary: Sets of bronze bells of graded size, each giving two pitches.

name: Keyboards with twelve fixed keys to the octave
summary: Organs, clavichords and harpsichords: every pitch is fixed when the instrument is tuned, and twelve keys must serve every scale.

name: Fretted lutes and viols
summary: A fret crosses all the strings, so each fret must serve as the same step on every string.

name: The abacus and the extraction of roots on it
Printing with movable type in Europe
Polyphony built on thirds and sixths
summary: Music in several parts in which thirds and sixths are treated as consonances and heard at rest.

name: Why some intervals sound consonant
summary: Two sounds together are sometimes smooth and sometimes rough: what makes the difference.

name: What the order of sound has to do with the order of the world
The circle of fifths does not close
summary: Twelve pure fifths overshoot seven octaves by a comma, so a scale made of fifths never returns to its first note.

name: Thirds made of pure fifths are harsh in harmony
summary: The major third of four pure fifths is wider than the pure third 5:4 by a comma, which is heard when thirds are held as consonances.

name: Playing in every key on one fixed tuning
summary: On twelve fixed keys a tuning that favours some keys leaves others unusable.

name: Placing the frets of a lute
summary: The frets must give semitones that serve every string and every key alike.

name: Consonance as a ratio of whole numbers
summary: The octave is 2:1, the fifth 3:2, the fourth 4:3: the consonances are the ratios of the first four numbers.

name: The harmony of the cosmos
summary: The order of the world is built on the ratios of the musical scale.

name: The twelve lü
summary: Twelve standard pitches within the octave, each with a name.

name: The twelve lü and the twelve months
summary: Each of the twelve pitches answers to a month of the year: the order of sound and the order of the seasons are one.

name: The twenty-two śruti
summary: The octave heard as twenty-two small steps, of which the notes of a scale take two, three or four.

name: The senario
summary: The consonances are the ratios of the numbers one to six, which admits the pure thirds 5:4 and 6:5.

name: Number as continuous quantity
summary: Roots are numbers like any other: there are no absurd, irrational or inexplicable numbers.

name: Temperament
summary: Any tuning that alters pure intervals a little so that a fixed set of pitches serves more music.

name: Pythagorean tuning
summary: A scale built from pure fifths 3:2 and octaves.

name: Sanfen sunyi
summary: Subtract a third of a length, then add a third, in turn: twelve pitches from one, each a pure fifth above or a fourth below the last.

name: Ptolemy's syntonic diatonic
summary: A diatonic scale with pure fifths and pure thirds, its tones of two sizes, 9:8 and 10:9.

name: Jing Fang's sixty lü
summary: The series of fifths carried on to sixty pitches, the fifty-fourth lying very near the first.

name: He Chengtian's new lü
summary: The twelve lengths adjusted by equal additions so that the series returns to its first pitch.

name: al-Urmawī's seventeen-tone division
summary: The octave divided into seventeen steps of two sizes, the limma and the comma.

name: Quarter-comma meantone
summary: Each fifth narrowed by a quarter of a comma so that the major thirds are pure; one fifth of the twelve is left a wolf.

name: Just intonation, as Zarlino taught it
summary: Ptolemy's syntonic diatonic taken as the natural scale of sung music.

name: Galilei's rule of 18:17
summary: Each fret placed at 17/18 of the string left: twelve nearly equal semitones.

name: Equal temperament
summary: The octave divided into twelve equal semitones, each of ratio the twelfth root of two.

name: Zhu Zaiyu's equal temperament
summary: The new method of exact ratios: twelve lengths in continued proportion, each the last divided by the twelfth root of two, computed to many places.

name: Stevin's equal temperament
summary: Twelve equal semitones by the twelfth root of two, set out in a manuscript not printed until 1884.

name: Well temperament
summary: Unequal temperaments of the keyboard in which every key can be used, each with a colour of its own.

name: Werckmeister's temperament III
summary: Four fifths each narrowed by a quarter of the Pythagorean comma, the other eight pure: the circle closes.

name: The bells of Marquis Yi of Zeng
summary: Sixty-five bronze bells buried about 433 BC and found in 1978, with inscriptions that name their pitches.

name: Timaeus
summary: Plato's account of the making of the world, whose soul is divided by the ratios of the scale.

name: Lüshi Chunqiu
summary: A compendium made under Lü Buwei in Qin, about 239 BC; its chapters on music give the generation of the twelve lü.

name: Nāṭyaśāstra
summary: The treatise on drama, dance and music ascribed to Bharata; its date is known only within centuries.

name: Harmonics
summary: Ptolemy's treatise, which tests the ratios of the scales by reason and by the ear together.

name: De institutione musica
summary: Boethius's Latin account of Greek harmonic theory, the textbook of music in the medieval quadrivium.

name: Kitāb al-mūsīqā al-kabīr
summary: al-Fārābī's Great Book of Music.

name: Kitāb al-adwār
summary: al-Urmawī's Book of Cycles.

# An outline of the dispute, drafted by a language model and unconfirmed.
exclusive question q1: In what tuning do voices sing when no instrument fixes their pitch?
position p1 -> q1: In Ptolemy's syntonic diatonic, with every consonance pure.
position p2 -> q1: In no scale of fixed ratios: voices temper their intervals as the music moves.
pro a1 -> p1: The ratios of the numbers one to six are the simplest, and the ear takes the simplest for the most consonant.
con a2 -> p1: In the syntonic diatonic the fifth from the second degree to the sixth is 40:27, a comma narrower than pure: not every consonance can be pure at once.
con a2 -> a1
premise a2: Its degrees are 1, 9:8, 5:4, 4:3, 3:2, 5:3, 15:8.
premise a2: From 9:8 up to 5:3 is 40:27, and 3:2 over 40:27 is 81:80.
conclusion a2: A scale of fixed pure ratios holds a consonance that is not pure.
